Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Pacifica Power Corp Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Pacifica Power Corp's Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
    2. Generation fleet performance and availability.
    3. Earnings per share performance and drivers.
    4. Customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial segments.
    5. Retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies.
    6. Grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects. On regulatory updates, we've secured strong approvals across our jurisdictions to support our capital plans—John will dive deeper into the specifics shortly. Our generation fleet delivered exceptional availability metrics, outpacing industry benchmarks—Lisa has more on operations. EPS came in strong, fueled by revenue growth and cost discipline—John again. Customer additions and usage are accelerating with electrification—also John. We're advancing plant retirements while building a cleaner replacement portfolio—Mike will cover strategy. And our grid investments are yielding real efficiency gains—Elena on tech.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss the financials.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.52 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.1 billion, primarily focused on transmission and distribution hardening and renewables plus storage. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 6-8% EPS growth through the decade.

Turning first to a detailed update on our regulatory rate case filings and outcomes, which are central to our financial planning at Pacifica Power Corp. These proceedings allow us to recover investments in grid upgrades, clean energy shifts, and resilience while serving our 4.2 million customers in California, Oregon, and Washington reliably.

We anchor our approach in multi-year rate plans tied to state clean energy goals like California's SB 100 for 100% clean power by 2045 and Oregon's 100% renewables by 2040. We've pursued cases in all three states for a $12.4 billion five-year capex through 2028—55% on T&D strengthening, 30% renewables and storage, 15% nuclear extensions and demand management.

In California, our CPUC General Rate Case filed last Q4 for 2025-2027 sought a $2.8 billion rate base hike from $14.2 billion to $17.0 billion, led by $1.9 billion in T&D for PSPS mitigation and undergrounding 1,200 miles in fire-prone areas like Sierra Foothills and Santa Cruz Mountains. This covers advanced insulators, LiDAR vegetation management, and 150 MW behind-the-meter batteries for microgrids.

The CPUC's September proposed decision approved 92% of our revenue ask—$1.15 billion yearly starting January 2025—with a 10.35% ROE, up 25 bps, recognizing inflation and equity risks. They greenlit 100% of our $450 million wildfire fund draw, including $200 million for drones and AI fault detection like PG&E pilots. We were disappointed by $120 million AFUDC disallowance on Desert Sun Solar delays and will appeal in November; final decision Q1 2025. This supports a 6.2% residential rate rise, funding 2.5 GW new renewables by 2030 for data center growth from Google and Microsoft in Central Valley.

In Oregon, serving 1.1 million customers, our 2024-2026 case wrapped last month with OPUC approving $650 million rate base growth to $4.8 billion, including $420 million for Columbia River hydro upgrades like $150 million fish passage at Bonneville Dam for FERC and NMFS compliance. This secures 1,200 MW baseload as we retire Boardman coal early by 2026. Wins: 9.8% ROE, full $80 million vegetation recovery from 2023 storms. $320 million annual revenue, 5.8% increase phased in. Next, 2027 IRP with 400 MWh LDES partnering Form Energy iron-air pilots for 40% wind.

In Washington, our biggest area with 2 million customers, June's transmission rider sought $900 million for 500 kV rebuilds Puget Sound to Idaho border amid NERC needs and 15% peak growth from EVs—load forecast 25% CAGR to 2030 from Boeing and smelters. October interim order gave 98%, with 10.2% ROE, 70/30 debt-equity, 11.5% T&D adders for ADMS like Avista/PSE. Unlocks $250 million yearly, offsetting 4% O&M inflation. Watching FERC Order 1000 for $5B Intertie, pushing cost allocation to load servers.

Federally, Q2 FERC accepted Diablo Canyon 200 MW nuclear uprate to 2045 per Newsom legislation, $300 million at 9.75% ROE for CAISO capacity amid solar curtailments. Advancing 1 GW battery-solar in CAISO queue for 2027.

Overall, 95% capex approval funds 85% of $2.5 billion 2024 program, 12% rate base CAGR. Monitoring CPUC decoupling at 2.5%, wildfire betas post-PG&E settlement. Benchmarking NextEra FPL, Dominion for 10%+ ROE. Risks: 11-month lags, TURN intervenors, but 20% settlements and IRA PTCs add 150 bps returns. Affirms ROE framework, de-risks $20B investments, full-year regulatory revenue +7.2%.

Next, on EPS performance and drivers. We delivered adjusted EPS of $1.52, up 11% from $1.37 last year, beating consensus $1.48 by $0.04. GAAP $1.41 after restructuring for Midwest fleet. Eighth straight double-digit quarter amid commodity swings.

Revenues hit $2.85 billion, +8%, from 6% weather-normalized retail sales to 28.5 TWh. Electrification drove residential/commercial +4%/7%; hyperscalers added 1.2 GW PPAs, 15-20% C&I CAGR like NextEra/Microsoft.

Regulated wins: PJM Pennsylvania $250M settlement 9.3% ROE +$0.08 EPS; ERCOT energy margins +22% to $145/MWh on 2.5 GW peakers.

O&M flat at $650M via Efficiency 2.0 AI maintenance cutting outages 18% to 3.2%, +$0.06 EPS. Fuel tailwind: gas $2.45/MMBtu -15%, 62% heat rate. Renewables 4.8 GW 95% factor, $120M PTCs offset battery O&M.

Northeast PJM/ISO-NE +14% on nuclear uprate 102% factor; Texas ERCOT +20% on 800 MW solar-storage PPAs $45/MWh; CAISO hydro down but gas capacity helped.

' Reliable Renewables': 70% $4.2B capex low-carbon, 1.5 GW renewables/600 MW storage, 35% carbon cut by 2027, CCUS, AFUDC +$0.04. FY24 EPS $5.95-6.15, Q4 $1.55-1.65. 85% hedged 2025 gas $2.80, FFO $2.1B, 65% payout, 6-8% CAGR.

Customer growth and usage trends also key. Added 45,000 net customers +2.1% to 2.18 million in Southeast/Midwest. Weather-normalized sales +4.8% to 28.2M MWh: additions + usage/customer 2.6% + weather 0.8 bps. Beats EEI 1.5%.

Residential: +1.8% to 1.65M on migration Florida/Georgia. Usage +3.2% to 1,045 kWh/month vs US 900, EV 4.2% pen, 12k heat pumps +15% winter. Midwest vortex +5%, SE CDDs +10%, peak 2,850 MW. AMI 65%, TOU shift 8% peak, load factor 61%. 3-4% growth, 5k EV chargers.

Commercial: +2.4% to 420k, usage +5.1% 9.8M MWh, data centers +12% 450 MW from Vogtle PPAs 95% PF. Midwest SMBs +7%. DR FlexPower 250 MW, BESS 120 MWh, load factor 62%. 6% growth, $150M data infra.

Industrial: +1.9% to 105k, usage +6.3% 8.4M MWh, EVs/semis Ohio 300 MW, steel/chem +9%, aluminum +15%. Hedged MISO-ERCOT, peak 2,100 MW. 25 MW microgrids H2. $2B commitments CPI+2%. 5-7% growth, rate base +7%.

Retail revenues +7.2% $2.1B, +60 bps EPS. $4.2B capex 40% T&D, load 3.5% CAGR.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. Let me provide an update on the operational front, starting with generation fleet performance and availability, which bolsters our reliability across our 25 GW portfolio of gas CC, nuclear, coal, hydro, wind, solar, and batteries in PJM, MISO, ERCOT, CAISO.

Q3 EAF 93.2%, +180 bps YoY, beat 92% target—third straight gain via outage management and health investments. Tops NERC GADS 91.5%, ahead of Dominion/Entergy.

Thermal 14 GW gas/coal EAF 92.8% +2.4 pts, forced outages 3.1% low via FleetWide Predictive Maintenance with GE Predix/Siemens MindSphere ML, -25% downtime on 7HA.02 like 1.2 GW Liberty Creek, heat rate 7,450 Btu/kWh.

Coal 10% fleet 88.5%, Dry Fork SCR NOx -15%, 90% CF. 800 MW coal-to-gas by 2026 EPA/state.

Nuclear 2.4 GW 93.8% CF #2 Exelon, Limerick +40 MWnet, Peach Bottom early robotic/Framatome twins. PJM BRA $45M $270/MW-day.

Renewables/storage 98.1%, wind 4 GW 38.5% CF Buffalo Ridge Siemens 5.X, solar 1.5 GW 26.8% Nextracker. Storage 1.8 GWh 99.2%, Gateway 400 MW/1600 MWh 4.2 cycles July, $12/MWh arb, no shed.

PJM 40% fleet zero outages 160 GW+ demand $450/MWh LMP. MISO hydro 1.2 TWh 97%. ERCOT gas 96% batt 250 GWh +20%. CAISO Palen 95% RTE.

$450M YTD enhancements +15%: H2 20% blend Cricket Valley 900 MW GE 7HA 2027 NY CLCPA; AspenTech digital $30M O&M e.g. HRSG leaks; 600 MW Colstrip coal-gas CCUS MHI 90%; post-Idalia microgrids/EV FERC 2222.

FY EAF 92.5-93.5%, Q4 light outages, renewables 30s CF, 5-7% EPS. Risks supply/LM6000, FERC capacity. 2.1 TWh clean, -1.4M tCO2e.

We're seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to predictive maintenance AI implementation. This has resulted in an 18% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

Mike Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, particularly the retirement of fossil fuel plants and our replacement approaches, which transform risk into returns in a decarbonizing world, optimizing rate base for 2030s EPS.

Our 4.2 GW coal (45 yrs avg subcritical), 1.8 GW gas peakers shifting per IRP Indiana/Ohio, PJM RTEP, EPA NSPS/ELG. EIA 15 GW coal retire 2024; we accelerate: 1,200 MW Greenfield full by 2027 early, 800 MW Riverbend thru 2029—50% coal, -25% Scope1 CO2 12M t.

Economics: $45/kW-yr FOM 10,500 HR LCOE >$70/MWh pre-carbon. Greenfield saves $180M Opex post-$250M decom (2x rev req). $120M MISO capacity to 2026 no stranding.

Replacements lift CF 55%→62%: $4.2B capex—

Renewables: 1.5 GW solar-storage IRA ITC+domestic, Prairie Sun 600 MW First Solar/Tesla 200 MWh $32/MWh 28% IRR 32% CF. 900 MW offshore JV Orsted Lake Erie 2029 $55/MWh.

Storage: 1.2 GW/4.8 GWh, Ohio 400 MW/1.6 GWh Form iron-air 100hr 85% RTE $15/kW-yr freq +$50/MWh arb.

Gas bridge: 1 GW CCGT, 400 MW GE 7HA.03 65% eff 30% H2 2028, SMR NuScale 200 MW 2032 $45/MWh 45V.

PJM data +15% ZMP renewables queue; ERCOT curtail hedge hydro RECs. Green bonds $2.5B 4.2%, 90% PPAs. Risks panels/CATL hedged, LOLP >15% NERC VPPs.

Exit 2024 2.1 GW net, 3.5 GW 2030 EPS neutral Y1 +8% cum. Like NextEra/Dominion 18x.

We are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Pacific Northwest market.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mike. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an AI-driven threat detection platform using Dragos to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, John, Lisa, Mike, and Elena. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for retirement of fossil fuel plants?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly, David. As Mike outlined, we're methodically retiring legacy coal like Greenfield and Riverbend ahead of schedule, replacing with low-cost solar-storage hybrids, batteries, and efficient gas—fully EPS accretive with locked PPAs and regulatory support. This de-risks our portfolio while meeting decarbonization goals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: What is your outlook for EPS next year?

John Ramirez: Thanks Emily. We guide FY25 adjusted EPS growth of 8-10% at midpoint, building on Q4 strength, hyperscaler loads, regulatory flows, and fleet efficiencies. Hedge book and contracted backlog provide clear visibility, risks balanced by liquidity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Greenlight Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning team. Could you drill down into your grid modernization and smart grid initiatives? Specifically, how these are impacting margins and what you're seeing in terms of ROI amid rising renewables penetration and regulatory pressures?

John Ramirez: Great question, Sarah, and one that's core to our long-term value creation in the regulated utility space. I'll take this one and then hand it off to our COO Lisa Chen for the technical deep dive.

At Pacifica Power Corp, grid modernization is a $1.2 billion multi-year capex program delivering strong returns, supporting ROE amid transition. Q3 added 450,000 AMI endpoints to 92% penetration for 2.5 million Northeast/Midwest customers. SAIDI down 28% YoY to 65 min vs EIA 112.

O&M savings $185M YTD: auto fault/veggie mgmt -22%, deferred $75M substations. DR EnergiGrid shaved 1.2 GW peak (15% Midwest)—$42M PJM capacity $250/MW-day. Ancillaries 14% EBITDA margin +5 pts.

Smart grid market $145B global 2030 12.5% CAGR DER/electrification. FERC 2222 opens DERMS 850 MW solar/batt/EVs NY/IL 8% LMP uplift.

Lisa Chen: Thanks, John. Our strategy pillars: sensing, automation, analytics, cybersecurity via GE Vernova GridOS.

Sensing: 5,200 PMUs/12,000 IoT sub-sec visibility, 97% auto fault isolate CAIDI -35% 92 min.

Automation: Schneider EcoStruxure ADMS FLISR 68% 34.5 kV feeders. Hurricane remnants 1.2 hr vs 4.5 regional—$28M credits NYSERDA.

Analytics: AI/ML 10PB data, Siemens MindSphere 92% transformer forecast -$110M 3 yrs. DLR 450 mi 138 kV +18% capacity wind 25% MISO.

Northeast NYISO/NEPool resiliency microgrids 15 sites Tesla 50 MW REV 11% IRR $300M. Midwest PJM/MISO hosting 1.8 GW solar +40% IEEE 1547.

Cyber: NERC CIP v6 100%, Dragos OT zero intrusion, Dominion threat share.

De-risks 15% EV load 300k chargers 2028 IRP, 40% renewables net-zero 2040. 2025 capex $450M 15-18% IRR, grid-service data centers.

Risks supply/labor eased CHIPS, lifts 5-yr EPS 200 bps.

John Ramirez: Perfect, Lisa. Sarah, does that address it? We're happy to follow up offline with our IRP deck. Operator, next caller?

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Pacifica Power Corp for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Pacifica Power Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
